human_tolerance.notes: A familiar bird in residential areas across the southern United States, singing by day and often through the night in artificially lit streets; it mimics car alarms, unoiled wheels and other artificial sounds as well as birds.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Pairs hatch about two to four broods a year; the female lays three to five eggs and incubates them for nearly two weeks (about 11 to 14 days), and both parents feed the chicks. Parental belligerence increases once the eggs hatch but not during the egg stage.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Males patrol a defended territory through the year, and the song is given day and night, so territorial display is not confined to the breeding season.

vocalizations.description: Long strings of varied phrases copied from other birds and from animals and artificial sources, including cats, dogs, frogs, crickets, unoiled wheels and car alarms. Imitation often fails to fool other birds even when convincing to humans, and it is used in male display and in territorial defence.

The 'hew' call, used by both sexes against potential nest predators, for chasing conspecifics and in interactions between mates. Of four recognised calls - nest relief, hew, chat or chatburst, and begging - chats are year-round while chatbursts occur only in the fall.

conservation.note: Wikipedia's speciesbox gives the IUCN 3.1 status least concern.

range.note: Wikipedia's range map legend distinguishes breeding summer visitors in the north, breeding residents in the south and non-breeding winter visitors further south, covering the United States, Mexico and Central America. Only the United States, Canada and Mexico are listed here, as the three countries where the article describes breeding or resident populations; the Central American wintering range is not itemised country by country.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia describes ground foraging on lawns and around buildings and perching on wires, shrubs and trees, with flight between them; walking and short hops are the authored mapping of that ground foraging, and gliding follows from the long tail and wing shape.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia describes the species as a territorial perching songbird that builds a nest and defends it against predators, and describes altricial chicks, but does not describe the nest structure in the sections used here; Cup is authored judgement from the perching-songbird habit.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 40-58 g body mass range.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 20.5-28 cm total length, which includes a tail almost as long as the body.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives a lifespan observed up to 8 years in the wild, with captive birds living up to 20. No typical wild value is given, so the observed wild maximum is used and flagged here.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia lists arthropods, earthworms, berries, fruits, seeds and occasionally flowers, small crustaceans and lizards, and states the diet is heavily animal prey in the breeding season with a drastic shift to fruits in fall and winter. The 50/35/15 split of invertebrate/fruit/seed is authored judgement across that seasonal shift.

traits.social.note: Territorial, with males patrolling and both parents feeding a brood; Pair is the mapping. The group-size upper bound is authored judgement, as some birds associate in small groups.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia describes daytime song and display and notes that the song is also given at night in artificially lit streets; Diurnal is the judgement mapping of its main activity.

traits.defense.note: The 'hew' call is used against nest predators and conspecifics, and both parents defend the nest; fleeing from a threat is the authored mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: unafraid in residential streets and gardens, foraging close to people, but it attacks predators near the nest.

habitat.use.note: The ground share follows the described lawn and building-side ground foraging for insects; the arboreal share covers perching, display and nesting.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored judgement: a shrub thicket is the nearest matching shelter for a territorial perching songbird that nests low.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the windows mark the breeding-season animal prey and the fall-winter shift to fruit that Wikipedia describes; nest and perch weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia describes the species as common in residential areas and records imitation of car alarms and other artificial sounds, and night singing in lit streets.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia gives northern populations as breeding summer visitors and southern ones as breeding residents, with northern birds wintering in the southern United States; it records no migration for the resident southern populations that include Georgia.

seasonal.phases.note: Brood number, clutch size and incubation length are from the Reproduction section; the month window is authored judgement, as the article gives no calendar dates; the territorial phase follows the year-round territorial display.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The article describes the young as altricial and immobile at hatching but gives no nestling period; the 60-day juvenile duration and scale are authored judgement for a songbird.

vocalizations.note: The four recognised calls, the hew call's uses and the chat/chatburst seasonal split are from the vocalisation section of Wikipedia; time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a grey back, pale underparts, dark wings with two white wing bars and white patches in the wings and tail, and a long tail nearly as long as the body. The shoulder patch and wing bars are authored judgement to render the bars the description names; tail_ratio follows the stated tail-to-body ratio.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag is 'invertebrate' because the diet is heavily arthropods and earthworms in the breeding season; flee_m is judgement.
